sentences.text: Crja/58/2022 on 8 November, 2024

Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal
 Office Notes,
Sl. Date reports,
No. orders or Court'S Or Judge'S Order
S  proceedings  or directions  and  Registrar's  order with  Signatures  IA No. 1 of 2022  In  CRJA No. 58 of 2022  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.

1. Ms. Neelima Mishra, learned counsel through Legal Aid for the appellant (via V.C.).
2.
Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. This is an admitted appeal, admitted on 07.03.2024.
Now, the Trial Court record has also been received and the paper book is prepared and supplied to the learned counsel for the parties.

5. Heard on bail application.
6.

The present appellant- Rohit has been convicted pursuant to the judgment and order dated 30.04.2022, passed by the Special Judge (POCSO)/District and Session Judge, Tehri Garhwal in Special Session Trial No. 10 of 2019, State vs. Rohit and another, whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced to undergo 3 years rigorous imprisonment with the fine of Rs. 5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 363 IPC, 5 years rigorous imprisonment with the fine of Rs.
10,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 366A IPC, 10 years rigorous imprisonment with the fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 376 IPC and 10 years rigorous imprisonment with the fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 5(l)/6 of the POSCO Act.

entities.text: Special Judge (POCSO)/District and Session Judge, Tehri Garhwal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: All the sentences shall run concurrently.

7. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant was arrested on 05.12.2019 and since then he is in jail and was never been enlarged on bail and as such is in long incarceration for last more than 5 years and 9 months and completed more than half of the sentence.
Learned counsel for the appellant also submits that the appellant has no previous criminal history.

CRJA/58/2022 on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93933080/
1 8.
Learned State Counsel has not disputed this fact that the appellant is in jail since 05.12.2019 and more than half of the sentence he has already completed.

9. After taking into consideration that the appellant has already completed more than half of the sentence and has no previous criminal history and there is no possibility that the appeal be expedited shortly, thus, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, this Court is of the view that the appellant deserves for bail.
10. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

11. Let the appellant be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
Realisation of fine shall also remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal.

12. List this case for final hearing in the month of August 2025.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 08.11.2024
